site.name: lumen-research
site.summary: Lumen Research — research assistant (local demo) Fictional research-assistant chat product. Local fixture for UXBench. Open `index.html` directly. Page `index.html` — Research thread Three-column layout: left rail for thread history, center conversation, right rail for Sources. Center column: - Conversation styled with serif body type. Each assistant turn renders inline citations as small chips (`[1]`, `[2]` …). Hovering a citation highlights and scrolls the matching source on the right; clicking jumps to it. - Embedded tables and lists are styled with the rest of the conversation.

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full lumen-research system, prioritizing the primary chatbot/agent interface flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The exploration achieved comprehensive coverage of the Lumen Research prototype across desktop and mobile viewports. On desktop, the conversational interface provides a clean layout with helpful features like expandable follow-up chips, though missing loading states and unresponsive utility actions degrade trust. On mobile, the experience degrades critically due to severe header overlapping, horizontal overflow, and an extremely compressed chat input field that makes drafting queries practically impossible.

exploration_plan.goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full lumen-research system, prioritizing the primary chatbot/agent interface flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_plan.summary: The exploration will start by testing the core chat interface, including typing in the textarea, using the 'Ask' button, and clicking suggested follow-up prompts. Next, it will validate header controls like 'Share thread', 'Export as PDF', and the 'Mode' selector. The run will then examine the left rail history links and the right rail sources panel, paying special attention to mobile responsiveness given the small tap target warnings flagged during prescan.
assumptions: As a static local demo, interactive features like exporting PDFs, sharing threads, or creating new threads may only display UI feedback (like alerts or state toggles) rather than performing full backend operations.
risk_hotspots: Left rail history links (flagged for small tap targets, high risk on mobile)
Mode selector in the header (flagged for missing label)
Integration between inline citations in the chat and the right rail sources panel

phases.title: Chat Input and Suggestions
phases.objective: Validate the core interaction of sending a message and using suggested follow-ups.
key_checks: Type text into the main textarea and click 'Ask'
Click one of the suggested follow-up buttons at the bottom of the chat
exit_criteria: Chat input controls and suggested action buttons have been interacted with and their visual/functional responses observed.

phases.title: Header and Mode Controls
phases.objective: Test the utility actions available at the top of the conversation view.
key_checks: Change the selection in the 'Mode' dropdown
Change the selection in the response length/type dropdown next to 'Ask'
exit_criteria: All header action buttons and dropdowns have been toggled or clicked.

phases.title: Thread History (Left Rail)
phases.objective: Check navigation between past threads and creation of new ones, assessing accessibility.
key_checks: Click multiple history links (e.g., 'EV battery recycling policy...', 'Trace prevalence...')
Verify tap target sizes visually on mobile viewport
exit_criteria: New thread initiation and history navigation have been tested.

phases.title: Sources and Citations (Right Rail)
phases.objective: Evaluate the research sources panel and its sorting/filtering capabilities.
key_checks: Change the 'Sort' dropdown in the Sources panel
Click the 'All' filter or similar tabs if present
Attempt to click an inline citation in the chat text to see if it interacts with the right rail
exit_criteria: Source panel controls have been manipulated.

coverage_targets.features: Test chat input, suggestions, header utilities, history navigation, and source panel sorting.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat phase 3 checks (Left Rail) on mobile to assess the severity of small tap target warnings.

notes: Pay attention to how the layout adapts when switching between desktop and mobile, as the three-column design may collapse or require off-canvas navigation.

findings.user_goal: Read the conversation history and access settings
findings.problem: Sticky header controls severely overlap chat content on mobile, rendering the conversation illegible.
findings.evidence: On the mobile viewport, elements like 'Share thread', 'Export as PDF', and the Mode dropdown float directly over the central conversation text and left-rail headers.
findings.why_it_matters: Visual overlapping destroys readability and makes it impossible for users to consume the research assistant's answers or navigate the interface cleanly.
findings.suggestion: Convert the top actions into a structured, solid-background sticky header for mobile, or move utility actions into a collapsible hamburger menu to save vertical space.

findings.user_goal: Draft a follow-up query on a mobile device
findings.problem: The chat input field is aggressively compressed horizontally on mobile.
findings.evidence: The mobile chat textarea is restricted to roughly 80px wide, forcing user text to wrap awkwardly (e.g., breaking 'afternoon-loaded' across lines), making input review very difficult.
findings.why_it_matters: Users cannot comfortably type, review, or edit their prompts if the text is constrained to a narrow vertical column.
findings.suggestion: Ensure the chat input container takes up 100% of the available viewport width on mobile, pushing inline settings like the 'Mode' dropdown to a separate row if necessary.
findings.source_hint: textarea[placeholder='Ask a follow-up, or paste a paper to summarize…']

findings.user_goal: View the interface comfortably on a smartphone
findings.problem: The page suffers from horizontal overflow on mobile viewports.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings report a page scroll width of 511px within a 390px viewport, indicating elements are breaking the horizontal bounds.
findings.why_it_matters: Horizontal scrolling on a primary vertical-scrolling conversational interface feels broken and leads to accidental horizontal swiping.
findings.suggestion: Set `overflow-x: hidden` on the body and ensure parent containers (like the three-column layout) use flex-wrap or switch to a stacked column layout via media queries.

findings.user_goal: Submit a question and wait for the assistant's reply
findings.problem: There is no system status or loading feedback after submitting a chat query.
findings.evidence: Clicking the 'Ask' button appends the user's message to the thread, but fails to display a loading spinner, 'typing...' indicator, or disabled state for the input.
findings.why_it_matters: Without immediate feedback, users might assume the system froze or their request failed, leading them to click submit multiple times or abandon the task.
findings.suggestion: Implement a clear 'typing...' skeleton state or a loading spinner immediately after a query is submitted.

findings.user_goal: Share or save the research thread
findings.problem: Utility buttons ('Share thread', 'Export as PDF') lack active states or functional feedback.
findings.evidence: Clicking 'Share thread' or 'Export as PDF' yields no toast notification, modal, or visual confirmation that the action was received.
findings.why_it_matters: Dead buttons degrade trust and leave users uncertain if the feature is broken, still loading, or unimplemented.
findings.suggestion: Even if the backend functionality is mocked, display a toast notification (e.g., 'Link copied to clipboard') or open a modal to acknowledge the user's intent.

findings.user_goal: Filter the sources panel by material type
findings.problem: Source filter tabs display an active visual state but do not actually filter the content.
findings.evidence: Clicking 'Books', 'Web', or 'Preprints' adds an active orange underline to the tab, but the list below continues to show mixed source types.
findings.why_it_matters: Providing a positive visual confirmation (the active underline) without executing the actual filtering logic creates a frustrating false affordance.
findings.suggestion: Connect the filter buttons to the rendering logic of the source list to hide non-matching items, or disable the buttons entirely if the feature is unavailable.

findings.user_goal: Understand and interact with form fields using assistive technology
findings.problem: Dropdown select menus lack accessible labels.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings highlight that the 'Mode' `<select>` (Balanced/Quick scan/Deep dive) and 'Sort' `<select>` lack an associated `<label>`, `aria-label`, or `placeholder`.
findings.why_it_matters: Screen reader users will not be able to identify the purpose of these dropdowns without contextual labels.
findings.suggestion: Add explicit `aria-label` attributes (e.g., `aria-label='Select response mode'`) or hidden `<label>` elements linked via `id`.

findings.user_goal: Select a follow-up question or source filter on a touchscreen
findings.problem: Several interactive chips and buttons have small touch targets.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings note that follow-up suggestion buttons (e.g., 'Walk me through pre-registering...') and source filters ('Papers', 'Books') have heights of 35px.
findings.why_it_matters: Touch targets below the standard 44px minimum increase the likelihood of misclicks, especially on mobile devices.
findings.suggestion: Increase the vertical padding on pill buttons and filter tabs to ensure a minimum height of 44px.

gaps: 62% of actions produced no visible URL/text change; this may indicate dead controls or repeated probes.
